name: Fairmont Le Chateau Frontenac
insider_take: This iconic castle-like fortress isn't just a hotel—it's Quebec City's crown jewel and one of the world's most photographed hotels, perched dramatically above the St. Lawrence River in Old Quebec's UNESCO World Heritage district.
whats_special: The Chateau Frontenac holds the Guinness World Record as the "most photographed hotel in the world" and served as the secret meeting place for Roosevelt and Churchill during WWII's Quebec Conferences. Its copper-green turrets and red-brick facade have dominated the Quebec skyline since 1893, making it older than the famous Hotel del Coronado.
pro_tip: Book a river-view room on the higher floors for breathtaking sunrise views over the St. Lawrence, and time your visit during Winter Carnival (February) when the hotel becomes the centerpiece of the world's largest winter festival.
dont_miss: The hotel's legendary Champagne Bar Sam for cocktails with a view, and step outside to explore the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Québec—you can walk to the famous Quartier Petit Champlain, North America's oldest commercial district, in just 5 minutes via the historic funicular or Breakneck Steps.
pros: Iconic castle-like architecture overlooking the St. Lawrence River
Prime location in Old Quebec's UNESCO World Heritage Site
Rich history as one of the world's most photographed hotels
Luxury amenities and world-class service standards
cons: Historic building may have smaller room sizes
